name: KPV

lead: KPV is a tripeptide (lysine-proline-valine) corresponding to the C-terminal end of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH). It retains anti-inflammatory activity without the pigmentation effects of the full hormone.

It is sold as a research chemical and discussed in peptide communities for gut inflammation, skin irritation and general "inflammation control." Almost all evidence is from cell and mouse models, particularly colitis, and no completed human trials support cosmetic or recovery claims.

paras: In preclinical studies KPV enters inflamed intestinal cells through the PepT1 transporter and dampens NF-κB and MAPK signaling, lowering pro-inflammatory cytokines. Its action appears to be partly independent of classical melanocortin receptors.

Human safety and efficacy data are lacking. Vendor products are unregulated with variable purity and stability. It is not approved as a drug, and self-injecting or ingesting unregulated peptides carries contamination and unknown-effect risks.
